title: Integrative spatial profiling of 3D genome organization and gene expression in tissue.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: GEO GSE311199 metadata and filelist.txt: 15 samples, one 687 GB RAW tar. Per-section Hi-C contact files (.nodups.pairs.gz) are 6.6-159 GB each (seven of the eight are 87-159 GB); combined HIC_RNA .h5ad.gz files are 340-515 MB (three sections only); RNA tar.gz files are 21-73 MB. Downloaded the Zenodo code archive (10.5281/zenodo.21475571, 45 MB): the notebooks show the Hi-C features used per spot are Higashi embeddings (a learned model's output) loaded from local .npy files that are not deposited, and one melanoma AnnData output of shape 6,268 spots x 2,000 genes.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Near-single-cell resolution, the tissues (mouse brain, E11.5/E13.5 embryos, human melanoma), and the compartment/TAD/loop findings come from the abstract only; full text returned HTTP 500 and the supplement was not retrievable. I did not open any h5ad, so whether the deposited h5ad holds binned Hi-C features is unverified.

a1_downloadable.note: Public on GEO with no login; checked the file listing. Individual files can be downloaded, but the Hi-C files are very large.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: For predicting expression from chromatin contacts, the label (RNA counts per spot) is a column in the processed RNA matrices. The input side is what has to be built (see A6). Seen only in the file names, not opened.

a3_inputs_present.note: Chromatin-contact inputs exist only as raw contact-pair lists (6.6-159 GB per section). The per-spot Hi-C features the authors used (Higashi embeddings, a model's output) are not deposited; this was checked in the code archive.

a4_units_stated.note: RNA is raw counts from STARsolo, a standard alignment-and-counting tool (seen in the code archive); not otherwise checked.

a5_enough_rows.note: One notebook output shows 6,268 spots x 2,000 genes for melanoma, but there are only 8 tissue sections, so the independent unit is small. Total spot count not verified.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: Roughly 0.8 TB of Hi-C contact files to build per-spot contact features (one section alone is 87-159 GB compressed)
a6_fits_laptop.note: Building contact features per spot requires streaming 100+ GB files per section with pairtools/cooler (tools for processing Hi-C contact files) on a cluster. This is well over the 5 GB limit, and there is no deposited processed contact matrix to use instead.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not checked; the full text was unavailable.

a8_label_provenance.note: RNA counts are a physical measurement. But the only ready-made Hi-C feature, Higashi embeddings, is a model output and is not deposited.

existing_models.name: scHiGex (graph transformer predicting single-cell gene expression from single-cell Hi-C, NAR Genomics and Bioinformatics 2025)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved in detail; trained on single-cell Hi-C plus RNA data (HiRES), not on spatial data.

existing_models.name: scGrapHiC (predicts pseudo-bulk single-cell Hi-C from single-cell RNA, Bioinformatics 2024)
Hi-Compass (predicts cell-type 3D genome from chromatin accessibility, including at spatial resolution, Nature Communications 2026)

backbone.name: None suitable; no open pretrained backbone takes spatial Hi-C input. scGPT (a single-cell model) would cover the RNA side only.
backbone.licence: GEO public data; code licence not checked

integration.partner_dataset: HiRES single-cell Hi-C+RNA (mouse embryo); 4DN/ENCODE bulk Hi-C
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does the link between contacts and expression learned in dissociated single cells hold in intact tissue? This would need the raw Hi-C processed first.

controls.positive_control: Recover A/B compartment-expression correlation (A compartments, the open and active part of the genome, are more highly expressed)

honest_claim_h3: With only 8 sections from 3 tissue types, a model could at best claim that per-spot contact features predict expression within these sections; spots from the same section are not independent.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use chromatin folding measured at each tissue spot to predict which genes that spot expresses.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-spot genome contact maps from 8 tissue sections (thousands of spots each, exact total unknown), which first have to be built from 100+ GB raw contact files.
plain_idea.predict: Per-spot RNA counts measured by sequencing on the same tissue section.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: It would show how much of the expression differences across a tissue the 3D genome explains.

ml_idea: Predict spot RNA from spot Hi-C features (or the reverse). This is blocked because the Hi-C input needs terabyte-scale processing.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from GEO file sizes only; nothing was timed. Higashi embeddings (the authors' Hi-C features) need a GPU.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Open one HIC_RNA.h5ad (340 MB) to see whether it holds binned Hi-C features. It probably does not, given that the code loads the Hi-C embeddings from separate local files.

verdict_reason: A6/A3 fail: the chromatin-contact inputs exist only as 87-159 GB raw pair files per section (about 0.8 TB in total), and the processed per-spot Hi-C features are not deposited. There are also only 8 tissue sections.
